title: decision: config keys experimental.decision.* with config-check
body:
## Goal
Add the `experimental.decision` config object (default, cloudflare, lean, fallback_pool, max_tries, max_repairs_per_answer, default_answers) and the config-check rules that make invalid settings fail loudly.

## Context
Design (on main once merged): `doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D5-decision-system.md` — read the section named below before starting.
Design §2.4 (default key) and §6.2 (ε ≤ δ). Config today has no decision key (baseline/v1-decisions-auto.md, 'Config surface').

## Exact files to change
- `packages/core/src/config (new decision schema beside model-routes.ts)`
- `packages/core/src/config/plugin/model-routes.ts (reference for keyed pool validation)`

## Approach
Schema with Effect Schema types. Config-check rules: `default` must name an existing route id; `lean.step <= lean.delta`; `max_tries` in {1,2}; `max_repairs_per_answer` in {0,1}; `fallback_pool` values must exist; `cloudflare.enabled` defaults false. A violated rule is a config error at load, never a silent default.

## Acceptance (each is a runnable check)
- [ ] Loading a config with `experimental.decision.default` set to an unknown route fails with a message naming the key.
- [ ] `lean.step` greater than `lean.delta` fails the config check.
- [ ] A config with no `experimental.decision` block loads and behaves exactly as V1 (no decision default, no lean).
- [ ] `bun test packages/core/test/config` passes.

## Test oracle
Reference: the config checks in model-routes.ts. Oracle: property test over random (delta, step) pairs — the config accepts iff step <= delta and both are in (0, 1].

title: decision: visited-set traversal over pools and leaves, cycle-skipped outcome, PBT
body:
## Goal
Walk decision pools with ONE visited set per call (AD6), covering leaves as well as pools, with the distinct outcomes cycle-skipped, already-processed, walled-skipped, budget-skipped and skipped-empty. Port the prototype's oracle to the fork as a property test.

## Context
Design (on main once merged): `doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D5-decision-system.md` — read the section named below before starting.
Design §8.1 (algorithm and outcome vocabulary), §8.2 (prototype and oracle). AD6 needs the leaf sentence (challenge C7): the prototype found a leaf reached through two pools attempted twice.

## Exact files to change
- `packages/core/src/config/plugin/model-routes.ts or the route expansion module that walks targets (locate the existing visited-set walk for fallbacks, brief §9 PR #9385)`
- `packages/core/test/route-traversal.property.test.ts (new)`
- `doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/research/prototypes/traversal.py (oracle reference, read-only)`

## Approach
Reuse the existing fallback walk's visited set; extend it so leaves are added to the same set. Outcomes: pool already visited → `cycle-skipped` (not failed); leaf already visited → `already-processed`; walled leaf → `walled-skipped` (never attempted); budget-closed leaf → `budget-skipped`; empty tier part → `skipped-empty`. Success ends the walk.

## Acceptance (each is a runnable check)
- [ ] Property test over >= 500 random graphs (seeded): no leaf attempted twice; no pool expanded twice; termination within pools+edges+1 visits.
- [ ] Property test: when no success occurs, attempted ∪ walled-skipped equals the brute-force reachable leaf set.
- [ ] No walled leaf appears in attempted, in any graph.
- [ ] A cycle never yields `failed`; a unit test with a two-pool cycle asserts `cycle-skipped` on the back edge.
- [ ] `bun test packages/core/test/route-traversal.property.test.ts` passes.

## Test oracle
Reference implementation: research/prototypes/traversal.py (already passing, 600 graphs). Oracle: brute-force BFS reachable set (no visited set) — equivalence, plus the invariant checks listed.

title: systemone façade: accept the standard body for routes and native providers; decision headers
body:
## Goal
Make `POST /v1/systemone` accept the standard body `{model, state, questions}` for decision routes (`opencode-route/decision*`) and native systemone provider models, pass native calls through, keep Clef behaviour unchanged, and return decision identity in headers only.

## Context
Design (on main once merged): `doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D5-decision-system.md` — read the section named below before starting.
Design §3.1 (accept and pass-through/adapt table), §3.2 (x- rules 1–5), §3.4 (failure modes), §3.5 challenges C2–C4. Today the door refuses everything but Clef (packages/core/src/systemone.ts:102) and forwards only {state, questions} (systemone.ts:240).

## Exact files to change
- `packages/core/src/systemone.ts (parseSystemOneRequest: widen the model grammar behind routing; keep the Clef grammar test)`
- `packages/server/src/handlers/completions.ts (the /v1/systemone handler; add response headers x-opencode-decision-id, -leg, -pool)`
- `packages/protocol/openapi.json (the systemone entry, around line 5704)`
- `packages/server/test/facade-parity.test.ts (pin the widened refusals as a documented change)`

## Approach
Parse: body must be an object (unchanged). Resolve model: a `opencode-route/*` decision route goes to the decision executor (D5-S05); a native systemone provider model goes to pass-through; a `@cf/cloudflare/clef*` model stays on the Clef path; anything else is 400 with the list of accepted models. Strip every `x-` key before any upstream call; ignore unknown `x-` keys (never 400). Response body stays the standard `{model, answers, usage?}`; identity in headers. Body x- keys only when the request sent `x-envelope: full`.

## Acceptance (each is a runnable check)
- [ ] A request with no x- keys reaches the native upstream with a body equal to `{state, questions}` plus the upstream model (check via the stub upstream).
- [ ] A request with unknown `x-foo` keys returns 200, not 400.
- [ ] A non-Clef, non-route, non-systemone model returns 400 with an accepted-models list.
- [ ] The Clef path returns the same bodies as V1 (facade-parity suite green except the pinned refusal change).
- [ ] Responses for decision routes carry `x-opencode-decision-id` in headers and no new body keys.
- [ ] `bun test packages/server/test/facade-parity.test.ts packages/core/test/systemone` passes.

## Test oracle
Parity oracle: the recorded pairs in packages/core/test/facade-parity.test.ts (the V1 contract). For the new routes: the standard response schema from packages/ai/src/experimental/system-one.ts (Response).

title: decision executor core: three input formats, output validator, ULID decision id, append-only gauges
body:
## Goal
Implement the executor core that every decision entry point uses: normalise the three input formats (F1 native systemone, F2 x-extended envelope, F3 compact question list) to one internal form; validate input; call the pool; re-validate the output; mint a `dec_` ULID; store the decision; accept append-only feedback gauges.

## Context
Design (on main once merged): `doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D5-decision-system.md` — read the section named below before starting.
Design §10.1 (formats F1–F3 and the F3 expansion rules), §10.2 (validator, ID, gauges). AD7: decisions and attempts are addressable events; feedback rows reference the ID and never rewrite.

## Exact files to change
- `packages/core/src/decision/ (new: normalise.ts, validate.ts, executor.ts, ids.ts, gauges.ts)`
- `packages/core/src/db/ migration: decision_record (id, created_at, pool, final_leg, default_used, tries, repairs, usage, ttft_ms, total_ms, prompt_id, prompt_version, prompt_date, x_tags, x_session, state_hash) and decision_feedback (append-only: decision_id, who, correct, wrong, created_at)`

## Approach
normalise(input): if `questions` is an object → F1/F2; if `ask` is an array → F3 expanded (choice array → criteria keyed by string, score array → criteria list, yn → noul, id → question id, q → instructions). Any other shape → `invalid-input` listing the three formats. validate(input): <=255 choice criteria; 2..10 score levels; unique question ids. Output validator re-checks the answer shape per packages/ai/src/experimental/evaluation-client.ts:46-83 and rounds probabilities to 2 decimals. ID: ULID with `dec_` prefix minted before the first call. `x-decision-id` reuse returns the stored decision.

## Acceptance (each is a runnable check)
- [ ] F1, F2 and F3 inputs for the same question set normalise to deep-equal internal forms.
- [ ] An input with `ask` as a non-array returns `invalid-input` and names all three formats.
- [ ] Re-submitting the same `x-decision-id` returns the stored decision and makes no upstream call.
- [ ] A feedback row inserted twice with the same (decision_id, who) is kept as two rows; no UPDATE statement exists for decision_feedback (grep check).
- [ ] `bun test packages/core/test/decision` passes.

## Test oracle
Oracle: a round-trip property test — for random question sets, F3 → internal → F1 reproduces the F1 input; the output validator accepts exactly the answer shapes in packages/ai/src/experimental/system-one.ts.

title: LLM decider: adapter, schema validation, failure taxonomy, two-try repair loop
body:
## Goal
Add the LLM-leg adapter: call a chat model with decision-llm v1 (D5-S16), validate the reply against the answer schema, classify failures (refusal, truncation, schema, business, provider), run the feedback retry (max total calls from config, default 2), renormalise sum-only business errors, then move to the next leg.

## Context
Design (on main once merged): `doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D5-decision-system.md` — read the section named below before starting.
Design §4.2 (prompt), §4.3 (schema), §4.4 (taxonomy and loop), §4.5 (options). R2 §3.3 for the feedback content.

## Exact files to change
- `packages/core/src/decision/llm-leg.ts (new)`
- `packages/core/src/decision/classify.ts (new: failure classes)`
- `packages/core/src/decision/feedback-prompt.ts (new: invalid output + compact schema + JSON-pointer errors + one hint)`

## Approach
Per leg: call; classify; if ok return. Business error that is only probability sum ≠ 1 with all values in [0,1] → renormalise, record `repairs += 1`, return. Refusal, truncation, provider → next leg. Schema or other business error → one retry with feedback prompt, while total calls < max_tries. Feedback prompt carries the invalid output verbatim, the compact schema, each validator error with its JSON pointer, one hint from a fixed table. Structured output (strict JSON schema) is used where the leg supports it (parameter, not policy).

## Acceptance (each is a runnable check)
- [ ] A reply with `confidence: 1.4` is classed `business`, gets exactly one retry, and the retry's valid reply is returned with tries=2.
- [ ] A reply that is valid JSON but sums to 0.97 is renormalised, counted in repairs, and makes no retry.
- [ ] A refusal makes no retry and moves to the next leg (asserted by call count).
- [ ] With max_tries=2, a leg never receives more than 2 model calls.
- [ ] `bun test packages/core/test/decision/llm-leg` passes.

## Test oracle
Oracle: a scripted fake model (golden replies: valid, invalid-schema, sum-only, refusal, truncated) with the expected classes and call counts; the schema checker is the reference validator from D5-S05.

title: default answers when every leg fails; fallback pool by effort
body:
## Goal
When the whole decision pool is exhausted, return the request's default answers (or config defaults, or the type default), with `default_used=true` and confidence 0; select the fallback pool from `x-effort` through `experimental.decision.fallback_pool`.

## Context

- `packages/core/src/decision/executor.ts (call site)`

## Approach
Resolution: per-question `x-default`, else `experimental.decision.default_answers[qid]`, else type default (noul → 0; choice → first criteria key with probability 1; score → lowest level), confidence 0. A question with no resolvable default is an error (500 with {error}); the config check requires a default for each type used.

- [ ] `x-default` overrides the config default for the same question.

## Test oracle

title: Cloudflare included-usage counter: UTC-day neurons, disengage before the call, pivot
body:
## Goal
Add `decision_budget(utc_day, provider, neurons)` and the budget-closed check that disengages the Cloudflare leg before the call when the UTC-day allowance (or the optional paid cap) would be exceeded, recording `budget-skipped` and pivoting to the next leg. Ship behind `experimental.decision.cloudflare.enabled` (default false).

## Context
Design (on main once merged): `doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D5-decision-system.md` — read the section named below before starting.
Design §5 (counter, algorithm, options B-a..B-d, the $10 wording §5.5), Q3 default. R2 §1.2 for rates (clef-flash 3,455 neurons per Mtok input; 10,000/day; reset 00:00 UTC; paid plan has no hard stop).

## Exact files to change
- `packages/core/src/decision/budget.ts (new)`
- `packages/core/src/db/ migration: decision_budget`

## Approach
estimated neurons = ceil(in_tokens × rate_per_Mtok / 1e6), in_tokens from chars ÷ 3.5 (ceiling) pre-call; row marked estimated=1. cf_leg_open(now): flag off → CLOSED (leg absent); used + est > cap → CLOSED; paid_cap set and used + est > paid_cap → CLOSED; else OPEN. A 429 or overage response never sets the cap; it is recorded as provider failure.

## Acceptance (each is a runnable check)
- [ ] With the flag off, the Cloudflare leg is absent from the walk (no budget-skipped row).
- [ ] With the flag on and used = cap - 1, a request estimated above 1 neuron is budget-skipped and the walk continues to the next leg.
- [ ] The counter resets at 00:00 UTC (test with an injected clock at 23:59:59 and 00:00:00).
- [ ] A 429 from Cloudflare does not change decision_budget.neurons except the estimated charge for the request.

## Test oracle
Oracle: a model-based test: a random sequence of (time, estimate) events against a reference counter in plain arithmetic; the leg is open exactly when the reference says so.

title: decision effort: x-effort, bounded additive tie-break lean, dependent-question sequencing
body:
## Goal
Implement the tie-break lean of design §6.2 (additive ε toward the lean target, only inside the δ band among the top two) and wire `x-effort` and `x-lean-order` through the executor. Absent `x-effort` has no effect.

## Context
Design (on main once merged): `doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D5-decision-system.md` — read the section named below before starting.
Design §6.1–§6.4. Options L-a..L-e (L-c chosen). Effort aliases xhigh/max/ultra/fast → high are applied in the resolver (brief §4, Q6).

## Exact files to change
- `packages/core/src/decision/lean.ts (new)`
- `packages/core/src/decision/executor.ts (call site, after validation, before return)`

## Approach
Pseudocode of design §6.2 verbatim: ranked by probability with ties kept in lean order; gap > δ → no-op; target index per tier (low 0, medium (n-1)//2, high n-1); pick the top-two member nearer the target (tie → the top one); add ε to that member; winner = argmax with the same tie rule. Record lean_applied and winner_before/after.

## Acceptance (each is a runnable check)
- [ ] With x-effort absent, the output equals the input probabilities bit-for-bit (no lean).
- [ ] With gap > δ, the output equals the input.
- [ ] xhigh, max, ultra and fast resolve to high before lean is applied (resolver test).
- [ ] `bun test packages/core/test/decision/lean` passes.

## Test oracle
Oracle: the guard in D5-S12 (property test). Reference implementation: the pseudocode in design §6.2, transcribed as a plain function in the test.

title: research: live probes of each decision door and M5 JSON validity for free fast LLMs

## Goal
Probe each decision door once and record status, typed-answer validity and latency: Zen jev-1.13-free (promo), TypeSafe jev-latest (only if a key exists by name), DeepSeek Flash off-peak, and the free fast LLMs (Groq, Cerebras) for JSON validity (M5). Record results with dates. No secret values in the record.

## Context
Design (on main once merged): `doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D5-decision-system.md` — read the section named below before starting.
Design §2.3 (evidence per leg), §9 (M5), §14 Q-l. R2 §1.8 marks Groq/Cerebras prices as third-party only.

## Exact files to change
- `research/decision-door-probes-2026-11-13.md (new, in the design folder)`

## Approach
One probe per door, using the probe body from baseline/v1-decisions-auto.md (the blue/table choice question). For LLM legs, ask the decider prompt v1 (D5-S16) for the same question and validate the reply against the answer schema. Never attempt a 100%-walled leg (standing rule): check route_usage first and record 'walled, not attempted'.

## Acceptance (each is a runnable check)
- [ ] Each door has one row: status, valid (y/n), latency_ms, date, key name used (name only).
- [ ] No walled door is probed; each skip is recorded with its route_usage reason.
- [ ] The file contains no key values (grep for `sk-` and `Bearer ` returns nothing).

## Test oracle
Oracle: the systemone answer schema (packages/ai/src/experimental/system-one.ts) — valid = the reply passes the same checks as D5-S05's validator.

title: trial: native vs cheap LLM per provider, 300–500 labelled decisions, cost per correct
body:
## Goal
Run the pre-registered measurement of design §9: replay 300–500 labelled historical decisions to each arm (Zen Jev free, TypeSafe Jev if keyed, DeepSeek Flash off-peak, gpt-5-nano if admitted, Luna 100k #medium as reference), 3× choice-order permutations, 10 repeats on a 20-item subset; decide by the pre-registered rule.

## Context
Design (on main once merged): `doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D5-decision-system.md` — read the section named below before starting.
Design §9.1 (method, metrics, decision rule, sample size) and §9.2. AD9: named trial, hypothesis, margin, review date, revert condition. Label source: D6 outcome schema.

## Exact files to change
- `research/trials/decision-native-vs-llm/PREREG.md (write before scoring)`
- `research/trials/decision-native-vs-llm/RESULTS.md (after)`

## Approach
Pre-register first: hypothesis, margin (5 accuracy points), n target, review date, revert condition, the correct-decision rule (not reverted and no rework label in 14 days). Then score. Cost per correct = Σcost ÷ Σcorrect with a Wilson 95 % interval on accuracy. Report n with every figure. Decision only if the interval does not span the threshold; otherwise record 'no decision, more labels'.

## Acceptance (each is a runnable check)
- [ ] PREREG.md is committed before any scoring commit (git log order check).
- [ ] RESULTS.md reports n, accuracy with Wilson CI, ECE after Platt fit (cross-validated), order flip rate, invalid rate, cost per correct, for every arm.
- [ ] The chosen order (native first or LLM first, per tier) is recorded with the rule that chose it.

## Test oracle
Oracle: the labels (D6 outcome rule) plus the pre-registered rule itself; calibration check ECE <= 0.05 as the native-acceptance threshold (R2 §7.1).

Rules: gh CLI only; merge commits only, never force-push main; CI on main only; secrets by name only; a 100%-walled leg is never attempted; code#9399 is an EPIC GUARD epic.

title: x-clauses: store the field, evaluate JsonLogic predicates over answers, effects in closed set
body:
## Goal
Accept `x-clauses` in the envelope (store it with the decision), evaluate the JsonLogic predicates against the answers so far using `json-logic-js` (or an equivalent JSON-logic evaluator, decided in the PR), and expose the effects as a list for V3 to apply. V2 applies no effects to the wire body.

## Context
Design (on main once merged): `doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D5-decision-system.md` — read the section named below before starting.
Design §7.1 (K-b chosen; K-a is the V3 gate), §7.3 (clause shape and effect set), §7.5 (superset rule, C5, C6).

## Exact files to change
- `packages/core/src/decision/clauses.ts (new: parse, evaluate predicates, list effects)`
- `packages/core/src/systemone.ts or the executor's envelope reader (store x-clauses)`

## Approach
Clause = {id, when (JsonLogic), then: [effect]}. Evaluate `when` with `var` over answers (answers.<qid>.choice, .probability, .noul, .score). Effects are parsed into a closed set (set, default, narrow, boost, rank, add_option) and rejected if outside it. Clauses are topologically ordered by the variables they read and written; a cycle is a compile error (cycle-error), never a silent drop.

## Acceptance (each is a runnable check)
- [ ] A clause with an unknown effect name is rejected at parse time.
- [ ] A clause cycle (A writes what B reads and B writes what A reads) returns cycle-error.
- [ ] Evaluating `when` with a missing answer does not throw; `missing` predicates behave as in §7.4.
- [ ] `bun test packages/core/test/decision/clauses` passes.

## Test oracle
Oracle: the eight vectors of D5-S19, plus a PBT over random JsonLogic trees checking that evaluation terminates (no loops in the language).

Rules: gh CLI only; merge commits only, never force-push main; CI on main only; secrets by name only; a 100%-walled leg is never attempted; code#9399 is an EPIC GUARD epic.

title: V3 clause compiler: apply effects to second-call state and bounded log-odds; CEL gate
body:
## Goal
Compile the V2 effect list into the second call's state (set/default), into candidate narrowing, and into bounded log-odds boosts (soft +0.2 nats, strong +1.5 nats, per-option cap ±3 nats). Gate: evaluate a CEL runtime for TypeScript (K-a) and record the decision.

## Context
Design (on main once merged): `doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D5-decision-system.md` — read the section named below before starting.
Design §7.1 (K-a as V3 gate), §7.3 (effects and bounds), R2 §4.3 (log-odds combination; design guesses to tune on labels).

## Exact files to change
- `packages/core/src/decision/compile.ts (new)`
- `packages/core/src/decision/clauses.ts (use)`

## Approach
Pure compile step: state' = state + answers of set/default; narrowed candidate set; boost vector b with |b_i| <= 3; probabilities p' ∝ p·exp(b) renormalised. Recorded as clause effects in the decision record.

## Acceptance (each is a runnable check)
- [ ] Each §7.4 example's effect matches its expected outcome (D5-S19).
- [ ] The cap ±3 nats is never exceeded (PBT over random clause stacks).
- [ ] With no clauses, the output equals the input.

## Test oracle
Oracle: D5-S19 vectors and the bound invariant; a CEL decision memo as the gate artefact.

Rules: gh CLI only; merge commits only, never force-push main; CI on main only; secrets by name only; a 100%-walled leg is never attempted; code#9399 is an EPIC GUARD epic.

title: V3 calibration: Platt or temperature per decision type and leg, versioned, raw and calibrated stored together
body:
## Goal
After >= 300 labels exist, fit Platt (binary) or temperature (multi-class) calibration per decision type and per leg, store raw and calibrated values with the calibrator version, and use the calibrated values for the lean and the thresholds.

## Context

## Exact files to change
- `research/calibration/ (new, fit scripts and reports)`

## Approach
Cross-validated fit; report ECE (10 bins), Brier, reliability diagram, selective risk. Version the calibrator; never overwrite a stored raw value.

## Acceptance (each is a runnable check)
- [ ] ECE after calibration <= 0.05 on held-out labels, or the calibrator is not used.
- [ ] Every decision record keeps raw and calibrated values and the calibrator version.

## Test oracle

title: V3 dependent questions: CPT for <=3-parent groups; conversation continuation by x-session
body:
## Goal
Add conditional probability tables for groups of at most three parent questions (design O15), and continuation of a conversation by `x-session`: prior answers carried into state as soft evidence (probabilities, not argmax).

## Context
Design (on main once merged): `doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D5-decision-system.md` — read the section named below before starting.
Design §6.4 (V2 sequencing), §3.3 (continuation scope), R2 §2.4 (chain rule; soft evidence).

## Exact files to change
- `packages/core/src/decision/cpt.ts (new)`
- `packages/core/src/decision/continuation.ts (new)`

## Approach
CPT over <=3 binary or ternary parents: table keyed by parent answers, learned or hand-set with a version. Continuation: the prior answers are rendered into state with their probabilities, never argmax alone.

## Acceptance (each is a runnable check)
- [ ] A CPT lookup returns the stored row for every parent combination; an unknown combination is an error.
- [ ] Continuation state carries probabilities (a test asserts the probability text is present).

## Test oracle
Oracle: the chain rule identity on a three-question toy distribution (joint = product of conditionals).
